requirements.requirement: Provide the supplied project documents through WebDAV at /documents/ on node1 TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: Authenticated GETs returned 200 for both supplied files, PROPFIND returned 207 and listed both names, served contents matched the preserved source hashes, and Apache was observed listening on port 8080 before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the editor account from access.txt to create, read, replace, and delete documents.
requirements.summary: A bounded authenticated test observed 201 create, 200 read, 204 replacement, correct replacement content, 204 deletion, and 404 afterward.

requirements.requirement: Honor exclusive document locks and prevent overwrites that omit the lock token.
requirements.summary: The successful assertions show LOCK acquisition, rejection of a tokenless PUT with 423, unchanged content after rejection, successful token-authorized replacement, unlock, and cleanup. The same behavior was directly reconfirmed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Prevent anonymous clients from accessing the workspace.
requirements.summary: Anonymous GET and PROPFIND requests returned 401 before restart, and anonymous GET remained 401 after recovery.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the initial project documents in /srv/legacy2/webdav-document-locks.
requirements.summary: Final SHA-256 hashes for brief.txt and budget.csv exactly match the prepared baseline, while the originals remained readable after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with that platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after observations both show Alpine 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts. Apache and its WebDAV dependencies came from the configured Alpine 3.23 repositories and operated successfully after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: it captures a healthy pre-restart service and data state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, listener, authentication, source data, and lock behavior. The only notable deficiency is uncleaned temporary evidence residue.
limitations: The lifecycle collector cannot query systemd failed units on Alpine; service health is instead directly demonstrated through OpenRC status, listener checks, and HTTP/WebDAV behavior.
The lifecycle temporary-file inventory is bounded, so the hygiene assessment can establish the listed residue but not exclude unobserved residue elsewhere.
Requirement source-preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Implementation mutations were causally connected to installation, configuration, correction of the missing DBM dependency, verification, or the required restart. CRUD and lock-test documents were deleted, and no unrelated service or package damage is evidenced. The hygiene defect is retained temporary residue: package logs and numerous WebDAV response/header files remained under /tmp. They were produced by the package and evidence commands and were not cleaned up; relevant producers include cmd-9fb9f27bcc074bf0, cmd-c6bb4bb9df194894, cmd-ec88a11d318949be, cmd-71e1bdb1c18b4898, cmd-38ab4862224f47ab, cmd-584498dacdf44ab3, cmd-022c1e72b2774060, cmd-23eb6a6818e64bfa, cmd-f11fb86e14cd43ff, and cmd-a7a4bd64b5204d80. This residue is low-risk but unnecessary and remained at final capture.
